description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of demonstrations and accuracy for different activation functions. The x-axis, labeled "#Demonstrations", has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1500, with tick labels at intervals of 250. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy", also has a linear scale, ranging from 45 to 55, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The plot displays four lines representing different activation functions: Squared-Exponential (dark blue, solid line, circle markers), Tanh (blue, solid line, circle markers), ELU (light blue, solid line, circle markers), and LLaMA-2-chat (pink, dashed line, no markers). The Squared-Exponential line starts at around 54 at 0 demonstrations and increases to approximately 56.5 at 750 demonstrations, remaining steady thereafter. The Tanh line begins at around 52.5 at 0 demonstrations, increases to about 55.5 at 500 demonstrations, and then remains relatively stable. The ELU line starts at around 47 at 0 demonstrations and remains relatively constant, ending at approximately 46.5 at 1500 demonstrations. The LLaMA-2-chat line remains constant at around 45.5 across the entire range of demonstrations.
